title: The Jenkins orphanage, Reverend Jenkins and White's baptism
summary: White describes the founding of the orphanage, Reverend Jenkins and his churches, and being baptized at fourteen.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: and that time I had come back home. How old an institution is the Jenkins orphanage?
The Jenkins orphanage was established I think around about 1890, I believe, by the Reverend Jenkins.
You knew him personally then, right? Well, I'm his son-in-law. Oh. I mean you'd known the family right there then before.

No, I didn't know anything about the family before. It happened that he was pastoring a Baptist church called the Siloam Baptist Church in King Street and also the Bethlehem Baptist Church about five miles out from King Street. In those days, the pastor could pastor more than one church if he felt able. If he gave one service here a month to this church and to another, I've known him to have as many as five churches in a circuit. Preach to one in the morning and another in the afternoon. So Mr. Jenkins was pastor of a big church in Charleston, but he accepted the pastor of both these churches on call from offices of the Baptist faith. And so- You were a Baptist then, were you? Well, no, I'm coming to that. I wasn't baptized until I was 14 years of age. At that time, I'm in the Jenkins orphanage in Charleston. My mother is dead now. Yeah. And I'm, I'm over to the orphanage now for a period until I reach manhood, I'm supposing. Well, I was baptized in what they call the Cooper River on this side and the Ashley River on this side of Charleston. Out here is the beach of the Atlantic Ocean. Well, we just weighed down into the beach as far as Mr. Jenkins would allow himself to be carried a little around the waist. I'd say a little above the waist, but not so it would be dangerous. And there's where I was baptized.
